lead.headline: US jets strike an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island, and Iran answers with drone attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain
lead.short: US fighter jets used precision munitions to strike a Revolutionary Guards missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island, an American official told AFP, calling it a response to Iranian "aggression targeting US personnel and assets". Kuwait and Bahrain said on Wednesday they had repelled air attacks, and Iran said its drones hit a US base in Kuwait.

why.text: The war is spreading back into the Gulf states after a lull, and an Indian sailor is missing after an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz.

more: Iran's army said its drones "targeted Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms" at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait. Bahrain has been targeted three times in five days, after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf states since September, and Qatar, a mediator, urged all parties to show restraint. Iran's IRNA said the US strike caused no serious damage.

India condemned an attack on 16 November on MT Tara Gas, a Panama-flagged LPG tanker in the strait. Of the 24 Indians on board, 21 were taken ashore at Khasab in Oman, two are in hospital and one is missing. "The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end," the external affairs ministry said.

facts.US target: IRGC missile launch site, Qeshm Island

update.new: US strikes Qeshm; Iran attacks Kuwait and Bahrain.
update.front: The war has flared again in the Gulf, with US strikes on Qeshm and Iranian drones over Kuwait.

seconds.headline: Nvidia's board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang, who will testify to Congress on 1 December
seconds.short: Nvidia's board does not intend to bring back Jensen Huang as chief executive, its chair said, a day after Trump said he would not mind his return. Huang will instead testify before three House committees on 1 December about "a potential breach of our national security", and general counsel Tim Teter will give a closed-door interview the next day.

why.text: It ends, for now, the campaign for Huang's return, and moves the affair to Congress, where the questions are about chips reaching China.

more: "The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia's role in allowing dangerous [People's Republic of China] actors to access our most advanced chips," said Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, who chair the foreign affairs, China and intelligence committees. They had warned Huang on 12 November that he could face a subpoena.

Alice Huang was executive director of Megaspeed, a Singapore cloud company that bought nearly $5bn of AI chips and helped about $12bn of chip sales in breach of US export controls, the Guardian reports. Malaysia is investigating whether it diverted chips. The Commerce Department opened an inquiry into Megaspeed in 2024, and the Justice Department took over in 2025.

update.new: The board rules out his return; he will testify.
update.front: Nvidia's board has shut the door on Huang's return, and Congress wants him on 1 December.

seconds.headline: Mary Peltola wins Alaska, giving Democrats nine Senate gains, their most in a midterm since 1958
seconds.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · AP · 18 NOV
seconds.short: Former congresswoman Mary Peltola has beaten Republican senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, the Associated Press projected, giving Democrats their ninth gain from a Republican-held seat in this month's midterms. It is the party's biggest midterm Senate gain since 1958, and gives it a 56-44 majority when the new Congress meets in January.

why.text: With both houses of Congress lost, Trump faces two years in which Democrats control his budgets, his nominees and the investigations.

more: In 1958, under Dwight Eisenhower, Democrats took 13 Republican seats and both of Alaska's new seats, a gain of 15. The new majority will be the party's largest in 16 years; Democrats last held 58 seats at the end of the 111th Congress in January 2011. Scott Colom's win in Mississippi had already given them an eighth gain.

Democrats have also taken the House of Representatives, gaining 42 seats as of Tuesday. The president's party usually loses ground in midterms, and second terms tend to be worse: in seven of the 16 midterms before this one, the president's party held or gained Senate seats, but all but one of those came in a first term.

update.front: Alaska gives Democrats a ninth Senate gain and a 56-44 majority.

seconds.headline: Security forces kill LeT militant Lateef Bhat in a Kulgam mosque after he refuses to surrender
seconds.short: Security forces killed Lashkar-e-Taiba militant Lateef Bhat, 22, who was hiding in a mosque in Zangalpora in south Kashmir's Kulgam, on Wednesday. The team tracking him came under fire from the mosque at about 3am. "We asked him to surrender but he refused," said senior superintendent of police Anayat Ali Choudhary, who said they had talked to him by phone.

why.text: Police blame Bhat for a string of attacks in south Kashmir this year, including two in July that killed a policeman and two migrant workers.

more: Police say Bhat and his accomplice Umar Nisar Dar, a baker who was killed two days ago at Kulgam's Laroo Bypass, attacked CRPF personnel in Akhran on 11 November, injuring three. CCTV footage released by security agencies suggested the two had surveyed several places together on 10 and 11 November.

Bhat was also behind twin attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July that killed a policeman and two labourers from Chhattisgarh, police say, and carried a reward of ₹15 lakh. "It's a big success, given the fact he joined in November last year," Choudhary said. "We exercised maximum restraint given he was hiding inside a mosque."

stories.headline: Ukraine's drone and missile strikes bring down a span of the Crimea bridge, which Putin once called a miracle
stories.short: Two back-to-back Ukrainian attacks with drones and missiles brought down a span of the road section of the Kerch bridge linking Russia to Crimea, and damaged the rail bridge beside it, the first strikes to do it major damage. Volodymyr Zelensky called it an "unprecedented operation". Russia has halted road traffic and restricted trains.

why.text: The bridge is Russia's direct link to Crimea, home of its Black Sea fleet, and a symbol of Putin's annexation.

more: Ukraine had attacked it before, with a truck bomb in 2022, naval drones in 2023 and explosives planted on its undersea pillars in 2025, without major damage. The 19-km bridge across the Kerch Strait, the longest in Europe, cost $3.6 billion. Putin opened it in 2018 by driving an orange truck across, saying "a miracle has come true".

Russia ordered it built straight after annexing Crimea in 2014, when there was no direct link between the mainland and the peninsula. Since the 2022 invasion Russia has also held a land corridor from the Donbas through Kherson to Crimea, so the bridge now matters as a symbol as much as for supplies.

stories.headline: The US makes data centres in five countries get licences for Nvidia chips, to stop China renting AI computing
stories.short: The US announced interim rules on Monday requiring data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to get a government licence to buy advanced chips from Nvidia and other American makers. The aim is to stop Chinese firms renting computing power abroad to train AI models, and to catch chips being smuggled into China.

why.text: China leans on overseas computing to get round US export bans, and the rules land days before Trump meets Xi in Shenzhen.

more: At least 30% of China's advanced AI computing power is projected to come from renting abroad or smuggling by 2027, according to the Institute for Progress, a US think-tank. China's foreign ministry called the rules "economic coercion" and said Beijing "will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests".

South East Asian countries have built many data centres, and some operators are accused of helping China evade the controls. Megaspeed, the region's biggest buyer of Nvidia chips, whose former director Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese spy, is accused of smuggling chips bought for Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. It denies wrongdoing.

briefs.headline: Google says attackers are now using AI to find and exploit software flaws with no human involved
briefs.text: Its threat group found a framework called exploit_agent on an exposed server. It compares code before and after a security patch, works out the flaw that was fixed, then writes and runs an exploit against systems not yet updated.

stories.headline: Waymo pulls its driverless taxis off freeways across the US after California calls them an imminent hazard
stories.short: Waymo has stopped commercial driverless rides on freeways in every US market where it offered them, after California's motor vehicles department temporarily banned its cars from the state's highways from 11 November. The pause also covers Phoenix, Austin and Miami. Waymo is still testing on freeways with trained specialists behind the wheel.

why.text: It is the biggest setback yet for Alphabet's robotaxi business, which completes half a million trips a week.

more: On 6 November a Waymo car on a San Francisco highway was filmed speeding towards and trying to pass two police cars whose flashing lights were meant to slow traffic behind a construction truck. On 5 November three Waymo vehicles drove into a construction zone in the Bay Area, which the company says caused no injuries or collisions.

The DMV said the cars' "recurring incursions" into active construction zones made driverless freeway operations "an imminent hazard to public safety", and that the ban will stay until Waymo shows it has taken effective corrective action. Waymo, which says the pause lets it "evaluate our performance", did not say how long it would last.

stories.headline: Pochettino ends his time with the US with a 2-0 win over Haiti, and leaves for Manchester United
stories.short: The United States beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati to reach the Concacaf Nations League semi-finals, 8-0 on aggregate, in Mauricio Pochettino's last match in charge. Christian Pulisic scored with an overhead kick and Julian Hall, 18, got his fifth goal in six caps. Pochettino now leaves for Manchester United, where his assistants have gone ahead.

why.text: He takes over a United side in a mess, a job the Telegraph calls a "dumpster fire".

more: Hall, a New York Red Bulls striker, doubled the lead in the 43rd minute. The US have now gone more than 400 minutes without conceding, last letting in a goal against Chile on 29 September. Neil Pierre, a 19-year-old centre-back, was cap-tied to the US by playing, ending any chance of him representing Haiti.

Pochettino's staff gave 77 players games over 25 months, a wide survey of the player pool that produced a 26-man World Cup squad and made room for young players such as Hall, Diego Kochen and Cavan Sullivan. He took over from Gregg Berhalter two years ago, and his time in charge was short and ended abruptly.
